new_claim.statement: For a base physical block K with P=B[K,K] invertible, S=Sc_K(B), T=S[I,J], h=rank(B[I,K]P^{-1}B[K,J]), and arbitrary symmetric rank-k E, A=B+E satisfies s_r(A[I,J])>=s_(r+h+k)(T). Hence s_(h+k+5)(T)>=sigma implies a continuous density with ||p_(X^TAX)||_infinity<=5e/(2sigma), independent of sizes/signs of E's eigenvalues and without any lower bound on actual Schur pivots.

mathematical_change: This removes the actual-pivot lower-bound hypothesis from the previous low-rank stability theorem whenever the base terminal cross packet has enough surplus rank. It supplies a direct aggregate-before-inversion certificate switch: pull the terminal base packet back to an original-coordinate cross block of A and apply the regularized determinant theorem directly.
partner_application: The account02/B12 Möbius stress family remains the exact pole test: when the surplus-rank hypothesis fails, its complementary physical three-coordinate theorem gives ||p||_infinity<=C_*/2 through scalar pivot cancellation. Thus the partner result and pullback theorem are complementary certificate switches.
unresolved_implication: The bare hypothesis s_3(A)>=1 still does not force an h+k+5 robust base cross packet, a noncollapsing pivot chain, or any single fixed certificate. Need an exhaustive product-preserving reduction combining pullback, physical pair/triple, ridge and grouped-bank mechanisms.
regularity: The pullback branch proves a continuous density vanishing at infinity; square-lift branches are only asserted essentially bounded unless separately upgraded.
